question.leadin: Answer the following about Eastern European leaders.
question.text: Elected president of Poland in 1990, this man is famous for organizing the famous Soviet trade union, Solidarity.
question.clue: His wife, Danuta, claimed his Nobel Peace Prize for him in 1983.

swap.leadin: One of this organization's posters shows a cardiogram leading into its name.
swap.text: Name this organization of union workers, led by Lech Walesa, that started a "self-limiting revolution". They protested at the Lenin Shipyard and various other places.
swap.clue: The first prime minister elected from this organization spoke of the "thick line" that would demarcate his policies compared to the past.

question.text: This capital of Poland sits on the Vistula and contains a statue of its coat of arms, a mermaid brandishing a sword, in its Old Town Market Place.
question.clue: This city was where Chancellor Willy Brandt appeared to spontaneously kneel in December 1970.

swap.text: The szlachta paralyzed this Polish-Lithuanian parliament with the liberum veto, which allowed singular noblemen to stop the legislative process.
swap.clue: The szlachta class composed the majority of its Chamber of Deputies.

question.text: At the same as the Gdansk shipyard strikes, a strike occurred in this town of Eastern Poland, the sight of a 1569 union creating the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Europeans who helped in the American Revolution.
swap.text: This Pole was promoted to Head Engineer of the Continental Army and helped fortify the American forces at Saratoga. He also led an uprising against Imperial Russia to protest the partitions of Poland.
swap.clue: This Polish engineer, military leader, and statesman. He was awarded U.S. citizenship for his role in the American Revolution, which included planning the defenses at the Battle of Saratoga.

question.leadin: An underground trade union in this country went on strike at the Lenin shipyards in Gdansk ("g-DA-eensk").
question.text: Name this country. Lech Walesa ("lek va-WEN-sa") became this country's first post-communist president, but he lost re-election to Alexander Kwasniewski ("kfash-NEV-skee").
question.clue: This country was joined with an eastern neighbor in the Union of Lublin.

swap.leadin: You are traveling the European Route of Industrial Heritage.
swap.text: You may encounter the Historic Silver Mine in Tarnowskie Gory, established by Duke John II of Opole and located in this region seized by Frederick the Great in the War of the Austrian Succession.
swap.clue: Frederick the Great's 1740 occupation of this region triggered the War of the Austrian Succession.

question.leadin: This event was engineered by Frederick the Great in order to avoid the expansion of a Russo-Turkish war.
question.text: Identify this 1772 agreement that enlarged Russia, Prussia, and Austria at the expense of about one-third of another country's territory.
question.answerHtml: the First Partition of Poland [prompt on partial answer]
question.clue: This event was made possible following a victory at Lanckorona by Suvorov over the Confederation of Bar, which had attempted to depose Stanislaw II.

swap.text: Algirdas's victory over the Golden Horde at the Battle of Blue Waters drove the greatest expansionary period of this polity, whose ruler Vytautus's involvement with the Samogitian uprisings and incessant warring with the Teutonic Knights helped prompt the Battle of Grunwald. For 15 points, identify this Grand Duchy which participated in the 1569 Union of Lublin.
swap.clue: This country which joined with its western neighbor in the 1569 Union of Lublin. In the 20th century, this Baltic state was the first to declare its independence from the Soviet Union.

question.text: The Janissary Revolt of 1622 followed a disastrous defeat at Choczim against this country, a combined commonwealth of two modern-day states ruled by the Jagiellon dynasty, with which the Ottomans had fought the Moldavian Magnate Wars. They often fought over Tatar and Cossack raids.
question.clue: A post-Jagiellonian king of this nation allied with Leopold I to break the 1683 siege of Vienna.

swap.text: Walesa attended one version of these negotiations that occurred in several countries between the Communist regimes and the opposition. In Poland in 1989, these talks resulted in semi-free elections and a victory for Solidarity.
swap.clue: Solidarity managed to get free elections following these talks. Talks of this name also occurred around the same time in such countries as Bulgaria and Hungary.

question.text: Mieszko conquered this former capital city that contained the Royal Wawel ("VAH-vel") Castle. Supposedly, a creature from this city named Smok Wawelski ("vah-VEL-ski") was tricked to eat sulfur-stuffed cow skins.
question.clue: Casimir III ruled from this city, which eclipsed early royal centers like Plock ("p'wotsk") and Gniezno ("g'nee-EZ-naw") after the pagan king Jogaila was baptized in its cathedral so he could marry the saint Queen Jadwiga ("yahd-VEE-gah").

swap.text: By declaring "I do not allow it," any member of the Sejm could invoke this heavily-abused right to defeat any measure under consideration, or to dissolve the Sejm and nullify all acts during its session.
swap.clue: The increasing frequency of this action led to the creation of so-called "confederated" bodies where this action was not allowed.

question.leadin: During this country's resistance to Russification, the Knygnesiai, or Book Smugglers, promoted its native language.
question.text: Identify this country that joined Poland in the Union of Lublin and whose capital is Vilnius.
question.clue: Another Grand Duke of this nation signed the Union of Krewo to marry Jadwiga of Anjou.

swap.leadin: The Dagome Iudex details much about this ruler's reign.
swap.text: Name this ruler who won the battle of Cedynia against Denmark. This father of Sigrid the Haughty may have performed one action to further his alliance with Boleslaw the Cruel.
swap.clue: This first duke and Christian ruler of the "Gniezno State" who was a grandfather of Canute the Great and a husband to Dobrawa. The Dagome iudex references this ruler's potential baptismal name.

question.text: The Essay on Diplomacy claims that nationalist movements would weaken Russia's influence, which this man supported with his "Prometheism" ideology. Czartoryski may have inspired this 20th-century Polish leader's plan to unite former Polish-Lithuanian lands into the "Intermarium."
question.clue: This victor at the "Miracle of the Vistula" made formal overtures to fellow Entente members suggesting his nation should regain control of Danzig.

swap.leadin: Spurred by threats from Russia in the Livonian War, this arrangement replaced the Union of Krewo, which established for only a personal union. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this 1569 agreement which united Poland and Lithuania into a single federation.
swap.clue: This pact which united Poland with a country to its east, signed in 1569.

question.leadin: Apocryphally, this dynasty came to power after the cruel Prince Popiel II ("POPE-yell the second") was imprisoned and eaten alive by rats and mice.
question.text: Name this dynasty that succeeded the Popielid dynasty. A history by Gallus Anonymus claims that this dynasty was founded by a namesake wheelwright with an always-full cellar, an ancestor of Boleslaw ("bo-LESS-waff") the Brave.
question.clue: Earlier, when this dynasty's ruler Henry II the Pious was killed at the Battle of Legnica, its Silesian branch was left exposed.

swap.leadin: Name these agreements that involved Russia and Poland, FTP each.
swap.text: In December 1618 the two nations signed this truce that ended Wladyslaw's campaign in Russia and suspended hostilities between the two sides for 14 ½ years.
